title: 5th July 2024 @ 1:08pm - Boarding Display & Meet the Accuser — Boarding Gate
subtitle: Boarding Gate
location: Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport (SCL), Santiago, Chile — Boarding Gate
classification: Attorney Work Product — Privileged and Confidential

participants.role: Latam Gate Staff — primary disputant, later accuser
Latam Gate Staff 2 — secondary staff, explains security crew delays

cluster_A_boarding_time_dispute.summary: Passenger asks about boarding status. Staff initially says 'es su presentación'. Passenger points out the display says 'embarcando'. Staff contradicts: 'ah no, en unos minutos'. The core semantic dispute — 'boarding' vs. 'presentation time' — is established.

cluster_B_definitional_battle.summary: Passenger questions what 'embarque' actually means and asks for documentation. Staff repeatedly insists 'esa es la hora de presentación' without providing written proof. Passenger escalates: '¿Hay alguna documentación explicándolo? Porque me parece que es distinto.' Staff's only defense is repetition.

cluster_C_delayed_flight_and_rushing.summary: Passenger reveals the flight arrived late, and he had to rush and fight with PDI to get to the gate on time. He expresses frustration that LATAM could notify passengers of delays via the app but doesn't. The boarding display shows 'embarcando' when boarding hasn't actually started — the system is misleading.

cluster_D_system_admission.summary: Staff admits 'en este minuto nosotros vamos a empezar el embarco' confirming boarding hasn't started yet despite the display. Passenger's math (12:35 + 40 min = 13:15 departure) is dismissed. Staff says the 40-min rule is disclosed at purchase, not on the boarding pass. Passenger calls the system 'estupido'; staff laughs and says 'Claro'. Passenger escalates to 'es como un engaño' (it's like a deception).

cluster_E_second_staff_intervention.summary: A second staff member intervenes, claiming 'ellos tienen otro tiempo' (the system shows a different time than the passenger's phone). Passenger counters that the correct time should be communicated to passengers. Staff 2 explains about waiting for the security crew. Passenger directly challenges: 'Pero tu entiende que no estas correcto?' Staff concedes: 'ah no po, no ta correcto' — an admission that the system is not correct.

cluster_F_pilot_closure.summary: Pilot Ruiz makes PA announcements welcoming passengers to flight A8159 to Brasilia and giving safety instructions. The recording ends mid-announcement.

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Boarding display showed 'embarcando' (boarding) when boarding had not actually begun — staff confirmed 'ah no, en unos minutos'
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: Supports pattern of misleading passenger-facing information systems

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Staff provided no written documentation to support the distinction between 'boarding time' and 'presentation time' despite passenger's direct request
Passenger had to 'correr y pelear con PDI' (run and fight with immigration) to reach the gate because the app showed boarding had started when it hadn't
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: Establishes emotional/physical toll caused by misleading boarding-time display

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Staff laughed and agreed ('Claro') when passenger called the system 'estupido' — implicit acknowledgment of the misleading practice
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: Staff admission of system deficiency; captured on recording

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Staff 2 admitted the system time differs from what passengers see: 'Ellos tienen otro tiempo al que le sale acá en su teléfono'
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: System-vs-reality discrepancy acknowledged by LATAM personnel

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Staff conceded the system was not correct: 'ah no po, no ta correcto'
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: Direct staff admission that the boarding-time display system is incorrect

key_evidentiary_findings.finding: Passenger characterized the boarding-time display practice as 'un engaño' (a deception) — a direct allegation of misleading conduct
key_evidentiary_findings.cross_reference: F-003 (manufactured pretext pattern) — the boarding-time display may serve as part of a broader system of passenger misinformation
